intent: Three oceans, one flag: the comparison that dwarfs the runner-up, the island count that explains it, then the walk nobody has done.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the LONGEST coastline?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the longest coastline?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Canada. 202,080 kilometres of coastline, on 3 oceans: the Pacific, the Arctic and the Atlantic.

lines.direction: ease back so all of Canada sits in frame; the three coastline columns rise on 'Indonesia' with Canada towering; an island sticker; the Russian flag-ball thinks on 'Russia'; Canada pulses on 'widest'
lines.text: Indonesia, with 17,000 islands, has about 55,000 kilometres. Russia, the widest country, under 38,000.

lines.direction: drift north over the Arctic Archipelago; a snowflake on 'Arctic'; the island counter runs to 52,455 on 'islands'; an ice sticker and the Arctic tag on 'ice'
lines.text: Most of Canada's coast is Arctic: 52,455 islands, many of them locked in ice for much of the year.

lines.direction: pull back to the whole country; a walking sticker on 'walk'; the 28 YEARS card on 'years'; the Canadian flag-ball grins; Canada pulses on 'nobody'
lines.text: Walk it at 20 kilometres a day and the full trip takes nearly 28 years. Nobody ever has.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Oceans on every side. Follow us.
